key_insight: YoCausal shows that current video generation models may look good at predicting motion, but still fall short of true causal understanding. It introduces a real-video benchmark to test whether models can detect when events violate physical or causal expectations.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the lack of realistic benchmarks for evaluating whether video diffusion models learn causality rather than just temporal statistics. Existing tests rely heavily on synthetic data, which does not reflect real-world complexity and suffers from a sim-to-real gap.
method: Builds YoCausal, a two-level benchmark based on the Violation of Expectation (VoE) paradigm from cognitive science.
Uses temporally reversed real-world videos as zero-cost natural counterfactual samples.
Evaluates whether video models can distinguish plausible event sequences from causally inconsistent ones.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers a more realistic way to measure progress toward world models. For practitioners, it helps reveal whether a model is learning genuine physical reasoning or only pattern matching from training data.
visual_elements: Side-by-side real video vs temporally reversed counterfactual video comparison

paper_title: YoCausal: How Far is Video Generation from World Model? A Causality Perspective
paper_authors: You-Zhe Xie, Yu-Hsuan Li, Jie-Ying Lee, Kaipeng Zhang, Yu-Lun Liu
